'''Hartmut Oschkinat''' (born 28 February 1957)<ref name=birthday60 /> is a German structural biologist and professor for chemistry at the [[Free University of Berlin]]. His research focuses on the study of biological systems with [[solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance]].

He is a member of the Editorial Boards of the ''[[Journal of Biomolecular NMR]]'' and ''[[Structure (journal)|Structure]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/physics/biophysics+%26+biological+physics/journal/10858?detailsPage=editorialBoard|title=Editorial Board of Journal of Biomolecular NMR|access-date=2017-02-14|archive-date=2016-08-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160805034320/http://www.springer.com/physics/biophysics+%26+biological+physics/journal/10858?detailsPage=editorialBoard|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cell.com/structure/editorial-board|title=Staff and Editorial Board of Structure|access-date=2017-02-14}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Oschkinat studied [[chemistry]] at the [[Goethe University Frankfurt|Johann-Wolfgang-Goethe University of Frankfurt]]. He received his doctoral degree in 1986 under the supervision of [[Horst Kessler]] with the title "Analysis of the conformation of Cyclosporin in solution using NMR-spectroscopy: development and use of new methods." in the field of [[nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy]] (NMR). After his work as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] with [[Geoffrey Bodenhausen]] at the [[University of Lausanne]], Oschkinat moved to the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in Martinsried in 1987 as a post-doc in the Lab of [[Marius Clore]] and Angela Gronenborn. There, he was working with [[G. Marius Clore|Marius Clore]], Angela Gronenborn and the [[Nobel Prize|Nobel]] laureate [[Robert Huber]]. After his habilitation at the [[Technical University of Munich]] in 1992, Hartmut Oschkinat moved to the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] in Heidelberg. Since 1998, he is the head of the department NMR-supported Structural Biology at the [[Leibniz-Institut für Molekulare Pharmakologie]] in Berlin.<ref name=fmpcv />

== Research ==
At the beginning of his career, Oschkinat worked in the field of solution-state NMR, and made fundamental contributions<ref name=Oschkinat1988 /> to establish the role of [[Nuclear magnetic resonance#Multi-dimensional NMR Spectroscopy|multidimensional NMR spectroscopy]] in [[structural biology]]. After using solution-state NMR spectroscopy to determine three-dimensional structures of soluble proteins such as the [[pleckstrin homology domain]]<ref name=Macias1994 /> and the [[WW domain]],<ref name=Marcias2000 /> characterise [[protein–protein interactions]] involving the latter,<ref name=Macias1996 /> with applications in [[fragment-based drug discovery]],<ref name=Joshi2006/><ref name=Pellecchia2008/> he moved on to focus on the investigation of biological systems by [[solid-state NMR]] (ssNMR) with [[magic angle spinning]]. His group was the first to solve a [[protein structure]] using ssNMR;<ref name=Comellas2013 /> the structure solved was that of a microcrystalline preparation of a [[SH3 domain]].<ref name=Castellani2002 /> Since 2005, his research group investigates complex biomolecular systems such as [[membrane proteins]] within the native lipid environment,<ref name=Hiller2005 /><ref name=Krabben2009 /><ref name=Shahid2012 /> [[amyloid]] fibrils,<ref name=Ferguson2006 /> and [[oligomers]].<ref name=Jehle2010 /> Moreover, he develops methods to address challenging questions in [[structural biology]] where ssNMR can be applied with particular advantages, and have made particular contributions to the development of [[dynamic nuclear polarisation]]<ref name=Geiger2016 /><ref name=Stoeppler2016 /> and proton detection using fast magic angle spinning.<ref name=Nieuwkoop2015 />

== Notable Achievements ==
* 1998: elected to membership of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]].<ref name=EMBOmember /> 
* 2009–2011: Acting Director of the [[Leibniz-Institut für Molekulare Pharmakologie]].<ref name=actingdirector /><ref name=actingdirectorend />
* 2012: International Scientific Review Board for the [[Central European Institute of Technology]] in Brno, Czech Republic.<ref name=CEITECscirev2012 /><ref name=CEITECintboard /> 
* 2013: elected to honorary membership of the National Magnetic Resonance Society of India.<ref name=NMRS2013 />
* 2014: one of six awardees of the [[Günther Laukien Prize]], awarded annually at the Experimental Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Conference in the USA.<ref name=Laukienlecturelist /><ref name=Laukienlecture /><ref name=Laukien2014Bruker /><ref name=Laukien2014BrukerResonance />
